 Judgment

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act 1989 against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

This case was already disposed off by this tribunal on 01.07.2020 and against the Judgment and Award passed by this tribunal, the petitioner has filed MFA No.2076/2021 before Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka for enhancement of compensation.

In the said MFA the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has remanded the matter to this tribunal by directing that the tribunal shall consider the material placed before this court and any other relevant material that would be placed by the parties before it by providing reasonable opportunity to both parties to adduce further evidence in respect of their respective cases and decide the matter afresh, in accordance with law.

03. The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that: That on 15022018 petitioner was going on his Motor Cycle bearing No.KA42U9527 from Halagur to Sathanur, when he reached near Government High School, Honnaganahalli, NH209, at about 11.30 a.m, the driver of Car bearing No.KA04MQ3627 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle from opposite direction.
As such petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and was immediately taken to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru.

He has been found with fracture of type III B open on the left and other injuries and has undergone surgery and took treatment as inpatient and incurred medical expenses of Rs.2,00,000/ and Rs.1,50,000/ towards other incidental charges and prior to accident petitioner was hale and healthy and was earning Rs.30,000/ p.m by doing work of Carpenter and after disposal of the case, during last week of October 2020 he developed severe pain in his left leg and hence, he got admitted to hospital on 04.11.2020 and the doctor after diagnosis found that there is nonhealed wound over left leg, abnormal mobility, decreased sensation over left foot ankle and severe infection had spread to the left leg and there is every chance that the infection may spread to the entire body, if the leg is not amputated at the earliest.

Hence, as per the advice of the doctor, he underwent operation and his left leg was amputated below the knee and incurred additional expenses for the treatment and because of amputation of left leg below the knee, he is permanently disabled and hence pray for compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 18% p.a and costs from the respondents.
04. On service of summons, the respondents have appeared through their respective counsels and filed written statement.

05. The respondent No.1 in its filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioner and contended that the claim made is exorbitant and their liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and further contended that the fact has been misrepresented, the Car driver was not negligent, but it was petitioner himself who was negligent in causing the accident and denied the Rajesh Alias Rajeshchari vs Advaith Motors Pvt Ltd on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87207830/

06. The respondent No.2 has filed written statement contending that the petition is not maintainable as it is based on false facts, the policy is valid and driver had the valid licence, there is no cause of action, the petitioner rode the motor cycle without licence and denied the age, avocation,
income and expenses details furnished by the petitioner and after remanding the matter, the respondent No.2 has filed additional written statement by contending that the petitioner is not entitled to grant additional compensation for the alleged amputation to the petitioner for the alleged accidental injuries.
The alleged accident has taken place on 15.02.2018.
The petitioner was examined as PW.1 on the earlier occasion and thereafter this tribunal passed the Judgment and award on 01.07.2020 and the said award was just and reasonable.

While he was examining as PW.1,
there was no evidence for the requirement of any amputation to by the petitioner or by the doctor on account of accidental injuries to the left leg.

When such is the case, how subsequently it has effected to undergo for amputation to his left leg due to the alleged accidental injuries and therefore, the alleged amputation probably for some previous history of his health conditions.
Therefore, there is no nexus between the alleged accidental injuries and the present amputation to his left leg.

Hence,
petitioner is not entitled for any additional compensation and the amount claimed is highly exorbitant without any base and hence, pray to dismiss the petition against them.
07. Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed by my learned predecessor:  ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 15 022018 at about 11.30 a.m., near Government High School, Honnaganahalli, Kanakapura - Malavalli Main Road, NH209, Sathanur Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing reg. No.KA04MQ3627 as alleged in the petition?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, from whom and at what quantum?
3. What Order or Award?
08.

In the earlier stage, in order to prove the case, petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to 14 and subsequently after remanding the matter, he produced additional documents as Ex.P.18 to 24 and on earlier stage the doctor who treated the petitioner and assessed the disability got examined as PW.2 and through him Ex.P.15 to Ex.P.17 documents are marked and subsequently after remanding the matter, the same doctor is examined as PW.2 by producing additional documents as Ex.P.25 and 26.
In the earlier stage the respondent No.1 got examined its Official as RW.1 and through them Ex.R.1 to 3 documents are marked.
Respondent No.2 has not lead evidence.
Even after remanding the matter, the respondents have not lead any additional evidence and not produced any additional documents.
Hence, respondents side further evidence is taken as nil.

Issue No.1: The petitioner in order to prove his case he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chiefexamination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein and after remanding the matter by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, the petitioner has filed additional affidavit in lieu of his further chiefexamination and has produced additional documents at Ex.P.18 to 24.

During the course of crossexamination by the respondent No.1 counsel he has stated that due to grievous injuries to his leg, there was a infection and puss, the doctor has removed his left leg below knee and denied to the suggestion that there is no nexus between the injuries and removal of his leg and further in the crossexamination by the respondent No.2 counsel he denied to the suggestion that at the time of filing of the claim petition his injury was healed up and denied to the suggestion that due to B.P and Sugar, which was caused infection and not due to accidental injuries and also denied to the suggestion that since he has not taken proper followup treatment regularly, the infection was developed and also stated that he has underwent surgery at Boss hospital and also denied to the suggestion that due to his disease, his leg was removed and not due to accidental injuries.

12. After remanding the matter, the doctor who is examined as PW.2 earlier has filed additional affidavit in lieu of his further chiefexamination and has produced additional documents at Ex.P.25 and 26.

In his chief examination he has stated that the petitioner has developed infected nonunion of left tibia with stiffness of foot and ankle with equines deformity and reduced sensation over left leg and he underwent below knee amputation and he has stated that petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 85% to the left lower limb which is 42.5% of whole body and also stated that petitioner need prosthesis for amputated limb and has produced OPD record and Xray.

During the course of crossexamination by the respondent No.2 counsel he stated that the petitioner was admitted at Victoria hospital first time on 15.02.2018 and on that date the petitioner undergone surgery.
On 04.11.2020 petitioner was again admitted and underwent below knee surgery and he do not know when petitioner was undergone above knee operation and he has not seen above knee operation documents.

Further, he has stated that because of nature of injuries,
petitioner sustained infection to leg.

Due to nature of injuries type III B compound fracture, vessels and nerves are damaged and he took decision for below knee operation and operation was conducted at Boss Speciality hospital on 04.11.2020 and also stated that the petitioner has no symptoms of diabetic and petitioner has no other disease and denied to the suggestion that there is no chances of infection at tibia.

Witness volunteers that there is a type III B fracture, hence, there is a infection and also denied to the suggestion that if high quality treatment has been provided, then there is no infection and also denied to the suggestion that due to negligence of the petitioner, there is a infection, stiffness and loss of sensation to his foot and ankle and also denied to the suggestion Rajesh Alias Rajeshchari vs Advaith Motors Pvt Ltd on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87207830/

During the course of crossexamination by the respondent No.2 counsel he stated that he was present when this accident took place, he was sitting by the side of the driver and their driver was going consciously, but the bike rider came in rash manner and dashed against their vehicle.

Further, in the crossexamination by the petitioner counsel he admits that the road at place of accident is not having divider, but there is white line in the middle of the road and admits that their Car was proceeding from Sathanuru towards Halaguru and the bike was coming in the opposite direction and denied to the suggestion that at that their vehicle driver in the course of overtaking the bus in rash and negligent manner has dashed against the twowheeler which was coming in the opposite direction on the left side of the road and denied to the suggestion that this accident took place due to negligence of Car driver.
14.
Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked 26 documents as Ex.P.1 to 26 on his behalf.
Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Sathanuru Police against the driver of the offending car.
Ex.P.2 is a copy of Complaint, which was lodged against driver of offending car for his rash and negligent driving and caused accident and causing grievous injuries to the petitioner.
Ex.P.3 is copy of Wound certificate which discloses that petitioner has sustained two injuries, out of them injury No.2 is grievous in nature.

Ex.P.4 is copy of Charge Sheet which was filed against the driver of the offending car discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against driver of offending car and the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending car and caused grievous injuries to the petitioner.
Ex.P.5 is copy of Spot Mahazar.
Ex.P.6 is copy of IMV reports which shows involvement of both the vehicle and both vehicles are damaged.
Ex.P.7 is Discharge summaries discloses that the petitioner was admitted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru, twice as inpatient due to accidental injuries.

Ex.P.18 is Discharge summary which indicates that even during the pending of the appeal and even after disposal of the case, he has developed infection and was admitted at Boss hospital, Bengaluru, on 04.11.2020 and discharged on 06.11.2020 and underwent surgery for his left leg.
Ex.P.21 is Xray.
Ex.P.23 is Photographs shows the amputation of left leg of the petitioner.
Ex.P.25 is OPD record of the petitioner and Ex.P.26 is Xray.

15. On going through the above oral and documentary evidence adduced and produced by the petitioner, which clearly establishes that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 15022018, at about 11.30 a.m, near Government High School, Honnaganahalli,
Kanakapura - Malavalli Main Road, NH209, Sathanur Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing No.KA04MQ3627 by its driver as alleged in the petition.
Therefore, the petitioner has proved the Issue No.1.

sentences.text: 16. Issue No.2:
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Motor Vehicle Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was aged about 37 years and was doing Carpenter work and earning Rs.30,000/ p.m and has incurred Rs.3,50,000/ towards medical expenses, food, nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges etc., and became permanent disablement.

17. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth and he has not produced any evidence regarding his avocation and income.
But he has produced Ex.P.13 Aadhaar card wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 01.01.1978 and the alleged accident occurred on 15.02.2018.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 40 years and the same is considered for calculating compensation.
As per Sarla Verma case the multiplier applicable is 15 and the same is considered.
18. As stated above with regard to avocation and income the petitioner has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the LokAdalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2018 to be taken as Rs.12,500/ p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.12,500/.
19.

According to the evidence of PW.2, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner has developed infected nonunion of left tibia with stiffness of foot and ankle with equines deformity and reduced sensation over left leg and he underwent below knee amputation and he has assessed permanent physical disability of 85%
to the left lower limb which is 42.5% of whole body.
However, considering the evidence of PW.2 and amputation of left leg below the knee of the petitioner, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 40%.
Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.7 and 18 Discharge summaries, according to which the petitioner was admitted to Victoria hospital and Boss hospital as inpatient for 126 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charge, special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.2,00,000/ under this head.
21. Pain and sufferings:

As per Ex.P.3 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 doctor and Ex.P.21 Xray, Ex.P.23 Photographs, Ex.P.25 OPD record and Ex.P.26 Xray and on account of accidental injuries petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and he has sustained amputation of left leg below knee.

Accordingly with regard to amputation suffered by him in the Rajesh Alias Rajeshchari vs Advaith Motors Pvt Ltd on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87207830/
6 accident, he is entitled for Rs.2,00,000/ under this head.

sentences.text: 22. Loss of income during laid up period:

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.12,500/ p.m and he has admitted in the hospital for 126 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast 12 months.

Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.1,50,000/
(Rs.12,500 x 12) under this head.
23. Medical expenses:
As per Ex.P.8 and 20 the petitioner has incurred medical expenses of Rs.81,601/. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.81,601/ under the head of medical expenses.
24. Loss of future amenities in life and unhappiness:

Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and amputation of left leg below the knee and the disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.2,00,000/ towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
25. Cost of artificial limb and its maintenance:

According to PW.2 doctor the petitioner need prosthesis for amputated limb and in this regard the petitioner has produced Ex.P.22 cost of Estimate issued by Esha Prosthetics and Orthotics which shows the maximum cost of artificial limb is Rs.6,30,000/, but during the crossexamination, PW.2 the doctor has stated that cost of artificial limb upto Rs.2,00,000/ in private hospital.
Therefore, cost of artificial limb and its maintenance, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.4,00,000/ under this head.

26. Loss due to disability and disfigurement: Since the petitioner has sustained amputation of left leg below knee and he is get disfigurement of his leg, hence, he is entitled for Rs.2,00,000/ under this head.
27. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:

sentences.text: 29. Therefore, while assessing the disability in the case on hand, the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the above cited decisions are taken into consideration.
30. Accordingly, I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.23,31,601/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
31. As already discussed above, the respondents have failed to prove their defence though they have examined RW.1, the employee of the respondent No.1 company and has produced Ex.R.1 to 3 documents.

As the insurance policy of the offending vehicle is valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the negligence is on the part of the driver of the Car, I am of the opinion that, the respondent No.1 being the R.C. owner of the offending car and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident,
respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay compensation of Rs.23,31,601/
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
32. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.23,31,601/ (Rupees Twenty three lakhs thirty one thousand six hundred and one only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
